claude.rationale: This is a debt-for-equity chapter 11 recapitalization in which control passes from the KKR/ITOCHU sponsor group to the second-lien Backstop Parties (T1 replace, majority of the seven-person reorganized board), while the underlying oil-and-gas business, legal vehicle, and assets remain in place. gap_45=0 because the slice documents that the operating oil-and-gas assets (T4) and the operations producing them stayed together: "expected its oil and gas operations to continue in the ordinary course" with trade creditors and vendors paid in full — product and process are not split. gap_56=0 because the operational substrate and the people running it moved together: existing management and indemnification for current directors/officers/employees were to "remain in place," and the CEO was retained on the reorganized board, so process and organization stay coherently aligned at closing.

grok.rationale: The RSA/term sheet structured a chapter 11 debt-for-equity reorganization in which oil-and-gas operations were to continue in the ordinary course and the operating assets remained with the reorganized Company, so the customer-facing asset layer (T4) and the processes that produce it (T5) did not separate at closing (gap_45=0). The same closing structure left trade creditors paid in ordinary course and existing management/indemnification substantially in place alongside those continuing operations, so T5 and T6 were not structurally decoupled (gap_56=0); board control shifted to lender/Backstop designees but that is ownership/governance replacement, not a process-without-people gap.

openai.rationale: The continuity-of-operations line states that oil-and-gas operations were expected to continue in the ordinary course, while the structural summary says the operating assets remained substantially in place; therefore, no product-versus-process mismatch is documented at closing. The governance line retained the CEO and existing indemnification for directors, officers, and employees while installing a newly allocated seven-person board, so organizational continuity was partial but coherently aligned with the continuing operations rather than structurally separated from them.
